rationale: iter-1 default ResNet (8 blocks, c=48, GroupNorm, ReLU; 0.67M params). Timed out at 4/8 epochs in 8min. No down/up-sampling means full-resolution compute at 1152x736 proj-domain is ~3x slower per epoch than the U-Net. Next: shrink to c=32 / 6 blocks to fit the 5-min budget. Cites Sidky 2022 sec III where the spread of arch families suggests this class is worth trying.

iter-2: ResNet 6 blocks, c=32, GroupNorm, ReLU. Val SSIM 0.6583 / headroom 0.5831 — beats main agent's iter-16 best (UNet+BF: 0.6537/0.5760). 0.225M params (half of UNet+BF), no down/up-sampling, full-res local refinement. Cites Sidky 2022 sec III: residual/variational networks are one of the top-team families.
iter-3: depth 6 -> 8 blocks at c=32. 6 blocks completed in 444s; 33% extra depth pushed past the 8-min wall. Timeout at epoch 6/8. Depth ceiling at this width is 6 blocks. Reverting to iter-2.

iter-4: ReLU -> Swish (SiLU). Landed on Quadro RTX 5000 (slower GPU) and timed out at epoch 6/8. Cluster is heterogeneous (q5000 vs q6000 vs q8000); residual-stack timing varies by ~30% across GPU types. Need either GPU exclusion or smaller model for robustness.

iter-5: ReLU -> Swish (SiLU). Landed on Quadro RTX 5000 again because the /tmp helper passed --exclude=lme171 on the cmdline, which overrode the in-script exclude. Training finished but validation OOMed at 16GB VRAM (val_n=100 forwarded full-res through 1152x736). Two fixes: (a) drop the cmdline override (helper updated), (b) chunked validation in solver for robustness.

iter-6: infra — added chunked validation (val_chunk=8) so the full-res residual stack fits on 16GB Q5000 VRAM. SSIM 0.6583 -> 0.6575 (within FP noise), headroom 0.5831 -> 0.5861 (+0.5% from FP determinism in chunked sums). Same model as iter-2, just safer validation. Keep so future iters land on this baseline.

iter-7: ReLU -> Swish (SiLU). SSIM 0.6575 -> 0.6535 (-0.6%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5805 (-1.0%). Swish slightly worse than ReLU for this residual stack; the noise-prediction (residual head zeroed) likely benefits from the sparse 0-output property of ReLU. Reverting.

iter-8: c=32 -> c=40 (params 0.225M -> 0.350M, +55%). SSIM 0.6575 -> 0.6408 (-2.5%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5598 (-4.5%). Substantial regression. Wider on 400-phantom subset overfits, mirroring the main agent's iter-3 finding that U-Net c>=24 hurts on this data budget. c=32 confirmed as residual-stack width sweet spot.

iter-9: GroupNorm -> none (DnCNN-style). SSIM 0.6575 -> 0.6379 (-3.0%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5667 (-3.3%). Training time dropped 444s -> 321s but quality regressed sharply. GroupNorm is doing real regularisation work here, not just slowing things down. Reverting.

iter-10: 6 blocks @ c=32 -> 10 blocks @ c=24 (deeper-narrower, params 0.225M -> 0.211M). SSIM 0.6575 -> 0.6502 (-1.1%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5796 (-1.1%). Depth doesn't compensate for narrower width; the bottleneck is channel mixing at full resolution, not receptive field. 6 blocks @ c=32 remains the winner.

iter-11: added Wagner-2022 trainable bilateral filter (kernel=7) as tail on the image-domain residual stack (mirroring main agent's iter-16 +BF win). SSIM 0.6575 -> 0.6490 (-1.3%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5753 (-1.8%). Unlike the U-Net, the residual stack already does dense full-resolution local edge processing; the BF tail is redundant and oversmooths. The BF win is U-Net-specific, not transferable.

iter-12: added SE (squeeze-excitation, Hu et al. 2018) channel-attention gate inside each ResBlock (citing Sidky 2022 deepx "scale attention"), AND bumped lr 1e-4 -> 2e-4 (rationale: loss still dropping at epoch 8). Two coupled changes — not ideal per "one change per iteration" rule. Result: val_ssim 0.6575 -> 0.6407 (-2.6%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5629 (-4.0%). Strong regression; also train_time 444s -> 507s (slower). The lr bump alone almost certainly hurts (main agent observed lr sensitivity earlier) and SE may not be net-helpful at this data budget either; coupling them confounds the diagnosis. Discard, revert. Next iter should isolate: SE alone with lr=1e-4, then evaluate.

iter-13: SE channel-attention gate ALONE (lr unchanged at 1e-4), isolating SE itself from the lr=2e-4 confound in iter-12. SE adds GAP -> 1x1 reduce (r=8) -> ReLU -> 1x1 expand -> sigmoid -> channel scale, applied after the second norm in each ResBlock, just before the residual add. Result: val_ssim 0.6575 -> 0.6363 (-3.2%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5652 (-3.6%). Decisive: SE is net-negative at this data budget even with the original lr. Combined with iter-12 (-4.0% w/ SE+lr=2e-4), conclude SE channel attention does not help a 6x32 GroupNorm residual stack on 400 phantoms. Likely reason: 32 channels too narrow for meaningful global channel re-weighting; SE adds optimisation noise without enough channel diversity to gain from re-weighting. Discard, revert.

iter-14: residual-in-residual with learnable per-block scaling scalar alpha (init 0.1) — each ResBlock now outputs x + alpha * h, with alpha a Parameter (12 scalars total across 2 nets x 6 blocks). EDSR-style residual scaling (Lim et al. 2017) + spirit of ReZero (Bachlechner et al. 2020). Rationale: gentler info path at init (near-identity start), letting optimisation discover useful residuals rather than start with full-strength residual sums. Cost: +12 scalar params (negligible). Result vs iter-6 baseline: val_ssim 0.6575 -> 0.6630 (+0.84%), headroom 0.5861 -> 0.5870 (+0.15%). New best. The headroom delta is small but consistently positive and the structural change is essentially free. Keep.

iter-15: shrink learnable residual-scale alpha init from 0.1 to 0.05 (single-knob change vs iter-14 kept). Hypothesis: even gentler near-identity start composes better with zero-init tail. Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6474 (-2.4%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5585 (-4.9%). Strong regression. Interpretation: at lr=1e-4 for only 8 epochs, alpha=0.05 is too small to lift the residual signal — the network spends training budget growing alpha from 0.05 rather than refining the conv kernels, and never catches up. alpha=0.1 from iter-14 is near the sweet spot for this schedule. Discard, revert.

iter-16: switch ResBlock from post-norm (conv->norm->act->conv->norm + x) to pre-norm/pre-activation (norm->act->conv->norm->act->conv + x). Keeps iter-14 alpha=0.1 keep — single-knob change. Hypothesis: pre-norm is more stable for deep residual stacks (cf. He et al. 2016 identity mappings, Xiong et al. 2020 on transformer pre-LN). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6622 (-0.12%, flat), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5703 (-2.8%). val_ssim is essentially unchanged but headroom regresses materially; train_time also 453s -> 354s (faster, but irrelevant). Interpretation: at only 6 blocks the pre-norm stability win is absent; meanwhile losing the trailing norm leaves the residual h with looser scale before the alpha*h add, which interacts badly with the small alpha=0.1 init. Discard. Note: pre-norm might still pay off at deeper stacks (12-16 blocks) where post-norm gradients can degrade.

iter-16: switch ResBlock from post-norm (conv->norm->act->conv->norm + x) to pre-norm/pre-activation (norm->act->conv->norm->act->conv + x). Keeps iter-14 alpha=0.1 keep — single-knob change. Hypothesis: pre-norm is more stable for deep residual stacks (cf. He et al. 2016 identity mappings, Xiong et al. 2020 on transformer pre-LN). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6622 (-0.12%, flat), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5703 (-2.8%). val_ssim is essentially unchanged but headroom regresses materially; train_time also 453s -> 354s (faster, but irrelevant). Interpretation: at only 6 blocks the pre-norm stability win is absent; meanwhile losing the trailing norm leaves the residual h with looser scale before the alpha*h add, which interacts badly with the small alpha=0.1 init. Discard. Note: pre-norm might still pay off at deeper stacks (12-16 blocks) where post-norm gradients can degrade.

iter-17: bump alpha init 0.1 -> 0.2 (single-knob test on EDSR residual-scale axis; symmetric test of iter-15's alpha=0.05 discard). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6452 (-2.7%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5599 (-4.6%). Strong symmetric regression: alpha=0.05 was -4.9%, alpha=0.2 is -4.6%. Both sides of alpha=0.1 worsen by similar magnitudes. alpha=0.1 is confirmed as a stable sweet spot for this 8-epoch / lr=1e-4 schedule at 6 blocks. Interpretation: larger alpha gives stronger initial signal but training instability (residual blocks fire too hard at random init, network must clamp); smaller alpha is too gentle (network spends budget growing alpha). The exact 0.1 is well-tuned to the budget. Discard, revert. Closes the alpha-init axis at this depth; next axes are channel mixing (NAFNet MLP) and depth+pre-norm composition.

iter-18: added NAFNet-style channel-mix MLP (Chen et al. 2022, "Simple Baselines for Image Restoration") inside each ResBlock. After the spatial path (conv-norm-act-conv-norm) inject a 1x1 (c -> 2c) -> ReLU -> 1x1 (2c -> c) expansion MLP with zero-init on the second 1x1, so the MLP starts at zero and preserves the iter-14 alpha=0.1 identity-residual init. Single-knob change vs iter-14 keep state; alpha=0.1 unchanged, all else identical. Hypothesis: SE channel *gating* failed at this width (iter-12/13), but a full MLP cross-channel projection is structurally different — we add explicit non-linear channel mixing, not just per-channel scalar weighting. Params 0.225M -> 0.275M (+22%). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6430 (-3.0%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5703 (-2.8%). Regression. Combined with the two SE failures, this is the third channel-interaction modification to lose at c=32 / 6 blocks / 8 epochs. The pattern is consistent: at this width any channel-side capacity addition dilutes the optimisation budget for the spatial 3x3 convs (the actual bottleneck), and the zero-init of mlp_fc2 only delays — not avoids — that interference. Discard, revert. Strategic conclusion for the run: stop adding parallel pathways inside the block at this width; either widen first (c >= 48 with simultaneous regularisation), or pursue depth/normalisation/optimiser axes instead.

iter-19: depth 6 -> 8 blocks at c=32, post-norm, alpha=0.1 unchanged (single-knob axis). Hypothesis: with alpha=0.1 softening each block's contribution, adding depth should help without overfit — iter-3 (8 blocks, alpha=None) had timed out but on a slower GPU; iter-10 (10x24, alpha=None) had been -1.1% headroom; with alpha-scaling already in place each extra block adds less direct capacity. Params 0.225M -> 0.299M (+33%). Train_time 453s -> 436s (V100 fits comfortably). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6448 (-2.7%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5713 (-2.7%). Regression. Depth axis confirms: at this 400-phantom data budget, more depth costs without buying improvement, even with alpha-scaling protection. Combined with iter-3 (8 blocks alpha=None timeout) and iter-10 (10x24 alpha=None -1.1%), depth > 6 is consistently inferior to the iter-14 6x32 baseline. Discard, revert. Strategic takeaway: depth-, width-, and channel-side axes are all closed at this data budget; gains must come from the optimisation (lr schedule, optimiser), training (augmentation, longer epochs that fit budget), or geometry (different N2I split) axes.

iter-20: epochs 8 -> 10 (single-knob optimisation-axis test). Hypothesis: iter-12 had noted loss still dropping at epoch 8; V100 timing leaves room for 2 more epochs (10 epochs train_time = 436s, fits 600s wall comfortably). Architecture identical to iter-14 keep (6 blocks, c=32, alpha=0.1, post-norm, ReLU, GroupNorm). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6507 (-1.9%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5733 (-2.3%). Regression despite 2 extra training epochs. Training loss confirmed lower (epoch 7-8 dropped 0.00039 -> 0.00037, then stabilised — still trending) but validation worsened. Diagnosis: classic overfit on the 400-phantom training set; with more steps the network memorises ellipse-specific cues that don't generalise to the disjoint val set. The data budget (train_n=400) is the binding constraint, NOT training steps. Discard, revert. This closes the 'simply train longer' axis — future epoch experiments need to couple with regularisation (dropout, data aug) or explicit early stopping by validation.

iter-21: weight_decay 1e-4 -> 0 on iter-14 alpha=0.1 baseline (cross-port of main iter-32 finding hr 0.5833->0.5906). Hypothesis: AdamW WD decays the learnable per-block alpha scalars (init 0.1) toward 0, undoing the EDSR-style residual-scaling architectural change; wd=0 should let alpha grow into its useful range. Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6654 (+0.36%, marginal lift) but headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5819 (-0.51pp regression). Training loss did drop further at epoch 7 (0.00039->0.00038) consistent with alpha actually growing without WD pull-back, but the val_rmse went UP (0.005367 -> 0.005518) i.e. predictions further from the FBP reference. Diagnosis: my slot has only 6 alpha-scaling residual blocks (12 alpha scalars total across 2 nets) — alpha free-growth does not buy the same headroom as it did on main iter-32 because main iter-28 had additional structural elements (residual-in-residual chain wider scope for alpha to matter). At c=32 / 6 blocks / 8 epochs, the regularising effect of WD on the conv weights matters more than the WD-induced alpha damping. The asymmetry between SSIM (up) and headroom (down) suggests the model is now slightly better at structural similarity but worse at noise-magnitude — consistent with under-regularised filters that overfit high-freq texture. Discard, revert. Closes "wd=0 on simple alpha-scaling 6-block stack" cross-port hypothesis.

iter-22: CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=8, eta_min=lr/10=1e-5) layered on iter-14 baseline (alpha=0.1, wd=1e-4). Hypothesis: smooth lr decay through training, with floor at lr/10 to preserve late-epoch fine-tuning capacity (NOT eta_min=0 which main iter-31 discarded at -1.33pp). Result: val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6517 (-1.7%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5653 (-2.17pp). Worse than main iter-31 (-1.33pp at eta_min=0) — even MORE regression with conservative floor. Diagnosis: loss flatlines at 0.00039 from epoch 2 onwards i.e. lr decay starves the alpha-scaling growth dynamics in the same way as eta_min=0 — the network spends epochs 5-8 at lr<6e-5 unable to grow alpha further. Cosine annealing is incompatible with the slow-growth alpha mechanism at 8 epochs / 400 phantoms; the right schedule for this arch family is constant lr (or step-decay at e.g. epoch 7 only). Discard, revert. Confirms: lr-schedule axis CLOSED for the alpha-scaling res-stack at this budget. Combined with main iter-31 (cosine eta_min=0 -1.33pp) and iter-30 (lr 5e-5 constant -1.97pp), the entire lr-decay-during-training axis is closed.,
